title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
source: Nature
abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

title: Interfacial redox mediation enables efficient, stable wide-bandgap perovskites for perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
source: Joule
abstract: A reactive co-adsorption strategy couples 4-carboxybenzenethiol with hole-selective molecules (HSMs) to build a redox-active buried interface in wide-bandgap perovskites. Redox shuttling converts I2 and Pb0 back to halides, suppressing ion-migration-driven phase segregation. The 1.79 eV sub-cell reaches PCE of 21.02% (VOC for 1.375 V) and shows T90 over 800 h at 65°C MPPT, enabling 27.5% monolithic perovskite-organic tandems.

title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
source: Nature
abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

title: Molecular regulation and recurrent evolution of fungal bet-hedging conidiation
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Bet-hedging (BH) mitigates risk in fluctuating environments by promoting phenotypic diversity within a single genotype. Fungi exhibit remarkable phenotypic plasticity, such as conidiation polymorphism. Here, we show that entomopathogenic Metarhizium species produce either monomorphic or dimorphic conidia, which exhibit marked size variation to support different BH strategies. The large cylindrical and small ovoid conidia produced by the same species possess complementary advantages that facilitate adaptation to different conditions. Large conidia are heavily pigmented, ultraviolet-resistant, and highly virulent, whereas small conidia, produced either on separate phialides or atop large ones, germinate faster and resist bacteria better. These complementary traits represent a classic, yet previously unsuspected, diversified BH strategy. Mechanistic analysis revealed distinct gene expression patterns between morphotypes, leading to the identification of a transcription factor and a lipid-droplet surface protein that play key roles in governing dimorphic conidiation and pigmentation. Phylogenomic reconstruction revealed that later-diverging species reverted to an ancestral, monomorphic medium-spore state, indicating a recurrence of the conservative BH strategy. Pairwise experimental evolution confirmed that monomorphic populations have a fitness advantage under fluctuating ultraviolet irradiation. Our findings establish the BH mechanism in conidiation and reveal evolutionary experimentation with reversion across fungal speciation.

title: Nanocatalytic modulation of thrombin-ferroptosis axis for efficient intervention of ischemic stroke
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Ischemic stroke represents a leading cause of global mortality. Current therapeutic strategies, including recombinant tissue plasminogen activator and mechanical thrombectomy, are constrained by suboptimal recanalization, high recurrence rates, and reperfusion injury. In this work, we initially identified elevated intrathrombotic thrombin as a critical mediator of fibrinolytic resistance and a driver of ferroptosis-related neuronal injury following stroke. To specifically target this thrombin dysregulation, we designed ultrasmall tungsten-based polyoxometalate (W-POM) nanodots capable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier. In addition to their specific reactive oxygen species-scavenging capability, W-POM nanodots primarily modulate thrombin activity and attenuate its pathological signaling. In both thrombin-induced and ischemia-reperfusion injury models, W-POM nanodots significantly improve neurological outcomes by directly suppressing thrombin activity and inhibiting thrombin-driven ferroptosis. Furthermore, W-POM nanodots remodel the thrombotic microenvironment and reduce neuroinflammation, thereby conferring robust neuroprotection. This study highlights the thrombin-ferroptosis pathway as a key mechanistic axis in stroke and introduces a nanotherapeutic platform for targeted thrombin modulation in ischemic stroke therapy.

title: Nucleophile–electrophile chemistry produces a stable interphase for long-Life anode-Less lithium metal batteries
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries (ALLMBs) represent the optimal cell architecture for maximizing energy density, yet their practical viability is severely hindered by poor cycling life. This limitation stems from the unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), which drives continuous parasitic reactions with Li metal and induces severe interfacial degradation. Here we report a nucleophile–electrophile bridging strategy to construct a robust, passivating SEI that enables long-term stable cycling of ALLMBs. By leveraging a nucleophilic substitution mechanism, electron-rich organic species derived from the solvent, acting as nucleophiles, are covalently bridged by electron-deficient, boron-centred electrophiles derived from the anion. This molecular-level integration overcomes the inherent fragility of the SEI organic phase, generating mechanically robust oligoborates that resist interfacial degradation, along with lithium fluoride (LiF) nanocrystals nucleated in-situ to facilitate rapid Li+ transport. The resulting oligoborate–LiF hybrid SEI enables highly reversible Li plating/stripping and remarkably extends the ALLMB cycling life by 12-fold, maintaining 80% capacity over 300 cycles. The superior cyclability is maintained even under stringent practical conditions (high cathode loading, lean electrolyte supply, and pouch-cell operation). This work establishes a fundamentally new paradigm in interphase engineering, paving the way for high-energy, reliable ALLMBs.

title: Room temperature giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect in TbMn6Sn6
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The anomalous Hall effect is the transverse voltage response in the presence of out-of-plane magnetization or non-zero Berry curvature, which, traditionally, is modulated by an out-of-plane magnetic field. Here we demonstrate a giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by coplanar magnetic fields in the quantum magnet TbMn6Sn6 at room temperature. The very large Hall conductivity arises in response to an applied in-plane magnetic field and results from the tilting of the ferrimagnetic axis of the Mn and Tb moments to the out of plane direction. With the in-plane magnetic field aligning the ferrimagnetic axis, the Berry curvature induced giant anomalous Hall effect is observed. Further, we show that the in-plane field induced AHE is more pronounced below the temperature induced spin reorientation, showing a 2π periodicity in angular dependent measurements. Unlike the in-plane Hall effect previously observed primarily at low temperatures, the AHE we observe here represents the largest room-temperature response reported in a single material. Our results reveal strong coupling between an in-plane magnetic field and out-of-plane Berry curvature, enabling new opportunities to engineer spintronic and quantum device responses at practical operating temperatures.

title: Photothermal-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Light-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol is constrained by insufficient broadband light utilization and inefficient CO2 activation. Herein, we achieve highly efficient photothermal hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst, in which MoS2 is anchored on TiO2 to form an intimate interface, and Au nanoparticles (NPs) are deposited on MoS2–TiO2. We demonstrate that the MoS2–TiO2 interface induces the formation of few-layered MoS2 and transfers electrons from TiO2 to MoS2. MoS2 serves as the primary active phase for CO2 hydrogenation, while Au NPs enhance photo-to-heat conversion via the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect, thereby collectively facilitating CO2 activation under mild reaction conditions. Under photothermal conditions at 120°C in a continuous-flow reactor, the catalyst achieves 13.4% CO2 conversion with 84.7% methanol selectivity, and maintains stable performance over 400 hours without observable deactivation, underscoring it among the most competitive photothermal catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.

title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
source: Nature
abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm−2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm−2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm−2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Polyanion‐Modulated Vanadium‐Doped Ammonium Iron Phosphate Framework from Spent LiFePO4 for Lattice Oxygen‐Participated Water Oxidation
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Promoting the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) offers an effective route to improving the efficiency of water electrolysis. However, achieving efficient LOM operation in structurally stable catalysts remains challenging. To address this challenge, we report a microwave‐assisted upcycling strategy using spent LiFePO
                    4
                    as a lithium‐deficient precursor. The cycling‐induced lithium deficiency facilitates structural reorganization into a polyanion‐modulated vanadium‐doped ammonium iron phosphate hydroxide hydrate (S‐VAFP) without residual Li‐containing impurities. The resulting S‐VAFP features a three‐dimensional polyanionic framework composed of FeO
                    6
                    octahedra vertex‐linked with PO
                    4
                    tetrahedra, forming one‐dimensional channels that promote electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This architecture tunes Fe─O covalency, weakens Fe─(O─P) linkages, and drives in situ reconstruction into a catalytically active amorphous phase, thereby facilitating lattice oxygen participation. Chemical probe experiments and
                    18
                    O isotope‐labeling DEMS further verify the AEM–LOM coupled OER pathway. Benefiting from this structure‐guided LOM activation, S‐VAFP delivers an overpotential of 250 mV at 100 mA cm
                    −2
                    with a Tafel slope of 47.2 mV dec
                    ‒1
                    . An assembled anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) cell achieves 1.72 V at 1 A cm
                    −2
                    with stability exceeding 1000 h. Overall, this work establishes polyanion‐mediated electronic modulation as an effective strategy for designing stable iron phosphate electrocatalysts with enhanced lattice oxygen participation.

title: Directed Perovskite‐to‐Fullerene Electron Shuttle for 27.2% Inverted Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Although C
                    60
                    is almost exclusively used in the electron transport layers of high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), its weak affinity and unfavorable energy level alignment with perovskite lead to weak contact and mismatch in the conduction band level at the perovskite/C
                    60
                    interface, thereby limiting further improvement of device efficiency as well as compromising device long‐term operational stability. We synthesized an
                    n
                    ‐type Pyridinium molecule, 2,7‐di(pyridin‐4‐yl)benzo[lmn][3,8]phenanthroline‐1,3,6,8(2H,7H)‐tetraone dihydroiodide (PPTHI), and used it as the interfacial electron‐selective contact in inverted PSCs. The pyridinium iodide head unit in the PPTHI anchored to the halide vacancies and coordinated with the exposed lead. Moreover, the π‐conjugated core renders desirable electron‐transport capability, and the
                    n
                    ‐type interfacial modulator can also serve as an electron shuttle between perovskite and the C
                    60
                    electron transport layer. The improved electron extraction, optimized energetic, and passivated top surface translated to reduced V
                    OC
                    losses, leading to a certified stabilized power output efficiency of 26.54% and a champion device with an efficiency of 27.2% and a fill factor of 87.17%. Moreover, inverted PSCs incorporating the electron shuttle maintained over 80% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking.

title: Operando Pressure Monitoring, EIS, and X‐Ray Imaging of Solid‐State Sodium‐Sulfur Batteries — Insights into Chemo‐Mechanical Degradation Mechanisms
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In this study, we introduce a multi‐modal
                    operando
                    platform that combines cell stack pressure monitoring, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and x‐ray imaging to unravel the chemo‐mechanical aging processes in sulfide‐based solid‐state sodium‐sulfur (ssNa||S) cells. Despite their promising theoretical capacity and resource abundance, the mechanisms that limit the full performance of ssNa||S batteries are still poorly understood. To address this issue, we employ a new multi‐modal
                    operando
                    setup optimized for solid‐state cells. By comparing cells with different electrolytes, Na
                    3
                    PS
                    4
                    (NPS), a multiphase electrolyte Na
                    2
                    S‐P
                    2
                    S
                    5
                    ‐NaCl (NPS‐Cl), and Na
                    3
                    SbS
                    4
                    (NSbS),
                    operando
                    over the course of 50 cycles, we monitor slowly evolving aging effects that are found to be correlated with the electrolyte composition. For NPS, the combination of low interfacial stability against sodium and reduced ionic conductivity causes the electrochemical activity to be concentrated in localized regions, leading to sodium plating‐like behavior as the dominant degradation mechanism. In contrast, the chloride‐containing NPS‐Cl enhances the interfacial stability and mitigates dendrite formation. These findings provide valuable insights for the materials development of sulfide‐based electrolytes for ssNa||S cells and demonstrate the capability of combined operando diagnostics to resolve complex chemo‐mechanical phenomena that influence solid‐state battery performance.

ABSTRACT

title: Direct Solar Storage and On‐Demand Power via Threshold‐Matched Silicon Photovoltaics and Dual‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Direct integration of photovoltaics with batteries is attractive for energy‐autonomous mobile platforms, but mismatched photovoltaic output and battery charging requirements, limited high‐rate capability, and low‐temperature degradation can necessitate intermediate power electronics and restrict burst‐power delivery. Here, a threshold‐matched silicon photovoltaic–dual‐ion battery (PV–DIB) architecture is demonstrated by directly coupling a voltage‐ and current‐tailored crystalline‐silicon photovoltaic module with a high‐voltage dual‐ion battery pouch cell. Under one‐sun illumination, the photovoltaic module supplies ≈72 mA at the battery charging threshold, enabling direct charging without intermediate power‐conversion hardware. This matching establishes two complementary operating regimes: solar‐sustained operation when photovoltaic current meets the load demand and on‐demand battery assistance when the load exceeds the photovoltaic input. The integrated system delivers a maximum power density of 11,430 W kg
                    −1
                    at 40.83 mA cm
                    −2
                    , maintains stable operation under drone‐relevant dynamic load profiles, and the DIB retains 5,088 W kg
                    −1
                    at −10°C. Indoor and outdoor flight demonstrations validate direct solar energy storage and burst‐power delivery, establishing threshold matching as a practical design strategy for power‐electronics‐minimized, energy‐autonomous mobile systems.

title: Broadband Aeolian Vibration Harvesting and Electrical‐Damping‐Induced Suppression via Triboelectric‐Electromagnetic Coupling Mechanism
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Overhead transmission lines have long faced dual threats: a scarcity of power for sensor nodes and fatigue caused by aeolian vibrations. To address these issues, this paper proposes a synergistic strategy that integrates energy harvesting with vibration suppression, transforming vibration energy dissipation into a coupled process of electrical energy conversion and vibration suppression. Based on this strategy, a triboelectric‐electromagnetic coupling device (TECD) is developed. By leveraging the complementary frequency‐domain characteristics of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) and electromagnetic generators (EMGs), as well as the electrical damping generated during the energy conversion process, the device achieves deep synergy between wideband energy harvesting and vibration suppression. Experimental results demonstrate that the TECD can stably charge a 47 µF capacitor to a 5.2 V supply threshold at any frequency within the 5–50 Hz range, reaching a peak output power of up to 287.28 mW. Simultaneously, the associated electrical damping effectively suppresses vibrations, reducing the vibration acceleration of the primary structure by 86% under 30 Hz excitation. Built upon this device, an integrated harvesting‐suppression‐sensing system is constructed, paving a new path for self‐powered state monitoring and structural protection of transmission lines.

title: Interface‐to‐Bulk Grain Regulation Enables Sb2(S,Se)3 Solar Cells Exceeding 11% Efficiency
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Antimony selenosulfide (Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    ) represents an emerging thin‐film photovoltaic absorber owing to the excellent stability, tunable bandgap (1.1–1.7 eV), and high light absorption coefficient (> 10
                    5
                    cm
                    −1
                    ). Hydrothermally deposited Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    solar cells have broken the 10% efficiency bottleneck, yet as‐prepared Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    films suffer from small grains (typically ∼400 nm) with abundant grain boundaries (GBs) that introduce dense defect states, inducing severe non‐radiative recombination and hindering further efficiency enhancement. Here we develop an interface‐to‐bulk grain regulation strategy to achieve ultra‐large (exceeding 3 µm) columnar grains spanning the entire absorber. This strategy combines buried‐interface Sb pre‐deposition to tailor initial hydrothermal deposition and rear‐interface Se‐mediated two‐step post‐annealing to drive grain coalescence and growth through a sequential infiltration‐reaction‐coalescence mechanism. We also found that this grain engineering also leads to the passivation of bulk deep‐level and interfacial defects, and optimized heterojunction band alignment, which collectively suppresses non‐radiative recombination and in turn delivers an ultralow open‐circuit voltage deficit of 0.483 V. Consequently, the ultra‐large‐grain Sb

                    3

                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3

title: A Spin‐Crossover Neutral‐Site Perovskite Ferroelectric
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Perovskites have emerged as a globally researched family of multifunctional materials, benefiting from their rich physical properties. However, despite extensive investigations into their ferroelectric and magnetic properties, the coexistence of ferroelectricity and spin crossover (SCO) within perovskites remains largely unexplored. Herein, by combining perovskites and coordination polymers (CPs), we designed the first perovskite SCO ferroelectric, [Fe(4‐ATA)
                    3
                    ]SiF
                    6
                    (4‐ATA = 4‐amino‐1,2,4‐triazole), which adopts an uncommon neutral site (4‐ATA). The order‐disorder transition of 4‐ATA ligands induces a 6/
                    m
                    F6‐type ferroelectric phase transition at 331 K, with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC/cm
                    2
                    . Notably, [Fe(4‐ATA)
                    3
                    ]SiF
                    6
                    exhibits a SCO transition at 253 K within the ferroelectric phase, accompanied by distortion of the FeN
                    6
                    octahedron. Moreover, we observed a switchable magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) signal during the SCO transition. Our discovery opens a new avenue for the design of SCO ferroelectrics and sheds light on the further exploration of CP perovskite SCO ferroelectrics.

title: Steric Effect of Branch Grafting Enables Highly Soluble and Stable Phenazines in Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Phenazine‐based derivatives demonstrated promising potential in aqueous organic flow batteries (AOFBs) due to their features of low redox potential and the capability to undergo a one‐step two‐electron redox reaction. However, the highly conjugated structure of phenazine reduces molecular polarity and limits the solubility in electrolytes. Herein, we introduced a branched chain to achieve a highly stable and soluble phenazine derivative for AOFBs. The branched structure can effectively suppress the
                    π
                    –
                    π
                    interaction of the phenazine conjugation system but also inhibit the hydrolysis of the ether bond by steric hindrance, which significantly enhances the structural stability. The AOFB using a 1.0 mol/L electrolyte of 2,2′‐(phenazine‐2,3‐diylbis(oxy))dipropionic acid exhibited a high discharge capacity of 45.5 Ah/L and a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.00017% per cycle, with stable operation for more than 42 days (1200 cycles). Furthermore, a pilot‐scale stack demonstrated excellent cycling stability, with negligible capacity degradation after 400 cycles. The outstanding AOFB performance suggests its promise for large‐scale energy storage applications.

title: Synthetic Control of Oxygen Transport in Ultra‐Low Density Amorphous Thin Films
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ion transport is a critical functional property of many energy and electronic materials. In noncrystalline materials, it is believed that ion conductivity depends on density and free volume; however, it is difficult to tune density by more than 1% through melt‐quench synthesis. In this work, we use physical vapor deposition to deposit HfO
                    2
                    thin films with over 30% tunability in density. Isotope tracing shows that the oxygen tracer diffusivity of ultra‐low‐density films is about three orders of magnitude higher than that of higher‐density analogs. Molecular dynamics simulations similarly demonstrate this ability to control oxygen transport via density and further show that correlation effects are a plausible contributor to the density‐dependent diffusivities. Our work reveals that the mass density is an important yet routinely unreported parameter controlling oxygen transport in amorphous materials. This principle opens a new design space for the synthesis of thin‐film ion conductors.

title: Gradient‐Engineered Hole‐Selective Contact Layers via Spatially Confined Annealing for Efficient Tin–Lead and All‐Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Hole‐selective contact layers (HSLs) govern charge extraction and interfacial energetics in perovskite solar cells, yet conventional designs are largely limited to planar architectures with homogeneous electronic properties. Such planar HSLs are insufficient for mixed tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites, where short carrier diffusion lengths require efficient three‐dimensional charge‐collection pathways. Here, a spatially confined molecular‐gradient engineering strategy is introduced to construct energetic‐cascade HSLs within mesoporous frameworks. A screened and optimized phosphonic‐acid self‐assembled monolayer, [2‐(7H‐dibenzo[c,e]carbazol‐7‐yl)ethyl] phosphate, is incorporated into a mesoporous indium tin oxide nanocrystal matrix. Spatially confined annealing drives directional molecular redistribution, generating a controllable bottom‐to‐surface concentration gradient. This gradient establishes continuous energy cascades and graded hole‐transport channels, while simultaneously modulating the crystallization of the overlying Sn–Pb perovskite to suppress nonradiative recombination. Single‐junction Sn–Pb perovskite solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 24.14%, and monolithic two‐terminal all‐perovskite tandem solar cells reach 29.56% efficiency with substantially improved operational stability. More broadly, this work establishes molecular‐gradient engineering in porous matrices as a versatile strategy for programming charge transport and interfacial chemistry in solution‐processed optoelectronic devices.

title: Spontaneous Emulsification of Long‐Chain Alkanes to Form Oil‐in‐Water Nano‐Emulsions
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Spontaneous emulsification (SE) of long‐chain alkanes (LCA) to form oil‐in‐water (O/W) emulsion (SE‐O/W‐LCA) holds significant promise for applications such as oil sands extraction. However, SE‐O/W‐LCA remains a long‐standing challenge due to the extremely low polarity of LCA and high oil‐water interfacial tension. Herein, we present a successful strategy for achieving SE‐O/W‐LCA based on the design of surfactant molecular architecture. Systematic studies on structure–activity relationship correlating the structure of surfactant molecular segments with SE performance lead to an optimized surfactant architecture that achieves an emulsification capacity approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional surfactants. A general design guideline of surfactants is established, requiring both high LCA solubility and large hydrophilic–lipophilic balance (HLB) values for efficient SE. Fundamentally, the integrated SE mechanism, involving reverse‐micelle diffusion, Marangoni‐flow and O/W droplet formation, is elucidated alongside the corresponding thermodynamic basis and kinetic evolution. Finally, the developed strategy is successfully applied to practical oil sands extraction that delivers state‐of‐the‐art oil‐solid separation performance as compared with previously reported methods. The proposed SE‐O/W‐LCA strategy, together with the understanding of surfactant design guidelines and underlying mechanisms, is anticipated to inspire future research on low‐energy emulsification and advance the widespread industrial deployment of SE technology.

title: Understanding Activation Energies of Dark Currents in Shortwave Infrared Organic Photodiodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The advancement of near‐infrared (NIR) and shortwave‐infrared (SWIR) organic photodetectors (OPDs) has been fundamentally hindered by high dark current, which is often considered an intrinsic limitation. This stems from the prevailing model where trap‐assisted thermal generation caps the dark current activation energy (
                    E
                    a
                    ) at half the material's effective bandgap (). Here, we demonstrate that this perceived limit is not fundamental and can be surpassed. By systematically engineering thick‐film devices to suppress trap‐mediated recombination and shunt pathways, we demonstrate a transition to a bulk‐limited, band‐to‐band‐like thermal generation regime. This allows the activation energy to approach the effective bandgap (
                    E
                    a
                    ≈ ), far above the  limit of trap‐assisted generation. Our findings provide a direct design principle for fabricating NIR and SWIR OPDs with substantially lower dark currents.

title: High‐Efficiency Solution‐Processed Sensitized OLEDs With Low Roll‐Off Enabled by Near‐Ultraviolet Emissive Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescent Polysiloxanes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Achieving solution‐processed high‐efficiency blue OLEDs with low efficiency roll‐off remains a challenge. In this study, a siloxane‐backbone engineering strategy is proposed to develop near‐ultraviolet emissive thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers that can multifunctionally serve as emitter/host/sensitizer for solution‐processed blue OLEDs. Benefiting from good film‐forming ability, balanced carrier transport and efficient exciton utilization, the non‐doped OLEDs based on the prepared TADF polysiloxane, PSiCzBN
                    1
                    mCP
                    9
                    , achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE
                    max
                    ) of 8.2% with an electroluminescence peak at 394 nm. Notably, two TADF polysiloxanes are further used as host or sensitizer in hyperfluorescence and phosphor‐assisted TADF‐sensitized fluorescence (pTSF) devices. The solution‐processed blue pTSF device exhibits a high EQE
                    max
                    of 35.7%, placing it among the one of the best‐performing TADF polymeric OLEDs reported to date. This work demonstrates that siloxane‐backbone engineering is an effective design strategy for achieving high‐efficiency solution‐processed blue OLEDs by regulating film morphology and excited‐state energy level, simultaneously.

title: Phase coding supports neuronal replication and enables combinatorial problem solving
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Darwinian neurodynamics posits that the brain searches large solution spaces through iterated cycles of variation and selection on competing neural representations. Testing this hypothesis requires a biologically plausible neural replicator: a mechanism that copies spatiotemporal signals faithfully enough to cumulatively improve good solutions, yet loosely enough to allow exploration. We show that phase-coded spike patterns constitute such a replicator. Spike timing referenced to a local field oscillation is compressed into a transferable spike train and reconstructed by coincidence with the receiver’s own field, without synaptic plasticity or a shared code key. As replication noise rises, the system crosses two thresholds. Below the first, faithful copying sustains patterns as dynamic memory. Between the two thresholds, pattern populations evolve. On two hard combinatorial benchmarks, the traveling salesman problem and NK fitness landscapes, neural replication remains competitive with standard search methods at a matched evaluation budget. Beyond the second, an Eigen-like error threshold, inherited information collapses. The network architecture tunes the exploration-exploitation balance: high-degree lattices, where local competition is stronger, exploit smooth landscapes, while low-degree lattices, where weaker competition preserves diversity, search more broadly on rugged landscapes. The framework predicts phase-locked information transfer and phylogenetic structure in replay, as well as a selective loss of combinatorial problem solving beyond the error threshold. These results indicate that a single neurobiological substrate can support memory, variation, and selection, and point to evolutionary dynamics as a candidate computational principle for cognition.

title: Wnts are endothelial cell–derived PKD1/PKD2-dependent autocrine/paracrine vasodilators
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Wingless/Int-1 (Wnts) are secreted glycoproteins and canonical Frizzled receptor ligands. Recent evidence indicates that some Wnts can also bind to polycystin 1 (PKD1), a large transmembrane protein which can couple to polycystin 2 (PKD2) to form a nonselective cation channel. The functional significance of PKD1, PKD2, and Wnt-mediated PKD1 signaling in native cell types is poorly understood. Here, we tested the hypothesis that Wnts regulate arterial contractility, investigated the signaling mechanisms and cell types involved, and examined the cellular source of vasoactive Wnts. Our data show that Wnt9b and Wnt5a are endothelial cell (EC)-dependent vasodilators. Wnt9b stimulates vasodilation via EC PKD1/PKD2, whereas Wnt5a acts via both EC PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors. Wnts stimulate endothelial nitric oxide synthase and small conductance Ca
                    2+
                    -activated K
                    +
                    channels in ECs to produce vasodilation. Wnt9b and Wnt5a are present in plasma and intravenous infusion of Wnt9b stimulates an EC PKD1-dependent reduction in systemic blood pressure. Intravascular flow activates angiotensin II type 1 receptors which, through G
                    q/11
                    and Porcupine signaling, stimulate ECs to secrete Wnt9b and Wnt5a. Wnts which are secreted by ECs in response to flow activate PKD1/PKD2 on ECs and this mechanism contributes to the flow-mediated vasodilation. In summary, we show that Wnts are autocrine/paracrine vasodilator proteins. Intravascular flow stimulates ECs to secrete Wnts, which then act via PKD1/PKD2 and Frizzled receptors on ECs to induce vasodilation.

title: Human retinal capillary network analysis using vascular interconnectivity optical coherence tomography angiography
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The human retina is perfused by capillary plexuses at distinct inner-retinal depths. Interconnections among these plexuses are critical for perfusion, but are difficult to quantify using 2D en face optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA). Diabetic retinopathy (DR) involves extensive microvascular remodeling, however the topological changes, especially at the interplexus level, are challenging to assess in vivo. We introduce Network Analysis using Vascular Interconnectivity (NAVI) OCTA, a framework that reconstructs the 3D retinal capillary network across the superficial vascular (SVP), intermediate capillary (ICP), and deep capillary (DCP) plexuses. The reconstructed macula-wide vasculature contains more than 10,000 vessel segments, and can be quantitatively analyzed using network representation. This method reveals a divergent alteration in interplexus connectivity in early DR: superficial-to-intermediate connections decrease, while intermediate-to-deep connections increase. This finding is consistent with previous histological studies, but is quantitatively measured in vivo in the human retina, opening the possibility for longitudinal studies of capillary remodeling. In addition to size-based metrics (e.g., vessel length or area), NAVI can quantify recurrent small-scale connectivity patterns (motifs). Finally, joint connectivity-hemodynamics analysis is demonstrated in eyes with DR, where capillary topology and flow speed can be quantified using a single OCTA acquisition. NAVI OCTA is a scalable, computational framework that supports analysis of retinal vasculature as a network and provides an in vivo approach to study capillary remodeling in early DR.

title: Influence of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The effect of noninertial dynamics on static quantum resource theories is investigated. To this end, we first show the equivalence between noninertial effects and a completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) map. In this formulation, the Unruh effect is equivalent to a bosonic amplifier channel. The effect of this map on a generic quantum resource is investigated by studying the role of the CPTP map on the three core ingredients of a resource theory, namely, the free states, the free operations, and the resource quantifiers. We show several general statements can be made about these three components of a resource theory in the presence of noninertial motion.

title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

title: Promises and pitfalls of community moderation on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Social media platforms have traditionally relied on internal moderation teams and partnerships with independent fact-checking organizations to identify and flag problematic content. Recently, however, platforms including X (formerly Twitter) and Meta have shifted toward community-driven content moderation by launching their own versions of crowd-sourced fact-checking—Community Notes. If effectively scaled and governed, such crowd-checking initiatives have the potential to combat misinformation as successfully as community-driven efforts once did with spam. However, moderating misinformation is inherently more complex: perceptions of truth are often shaped by personal biases, political leanings, and cultural contexts, complicating consensus on what constitutes misleading content. This suggests that community efforts, while valuable, cannot replace the indispensable role of professional fact-checkers. Here we explore the emerging role of community-driven moderation, critically evaluate both the promises and the challenges of Community Notes at scale, and identify how collaborative and technical innovations can integrate the two distinct approaches.

title: Unsupervised Bayesian neural networks enable inference of complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Birth–death models quantify macroevolutionary and epidemiological processes, including speciation, extinction, and transmission, based on phylogenetic trees. Extensions of these models incorporate external covariates as predictors of these parameters, for instance linking traits or environmental variables with changes in these rates. However, the dependencies between predictors and model parameters are typically restricted to linear, additive effects and may thus fail to capture complex, nonlinear relationships underlying evolutionary dynamics. To address this limitation, we propose a framework that leverages unsupervised Bayesian neural networks to flexibly model functional relationships between these parameters and a broad set of predictors, including categorical traits, quantitative variables, and time series data. Based on these covariates, the network weights and thus the resulting birth–death dynamics are estimated jointly with the phylogenetic tree, obtained directly from sequence alignment data. Extensive simulations show that this approach accurately recovers predictor–parameter relationships, mitigates overfitting, and remains robust across both macroevolutionary and epidemiological contexts. Using explainable AI, we further show that our framework reliably identifies the most influential predictors and yields interpretable descriptions of their impact on the inferred rates. Finally, we apply our method in two empirical analyses: linking SARS-CoV-2 migration dynamics with travel data during its early spread in Europe, and inferring trait- and time-dependent speciation and extinction rates in the diversification of platyrrhines. Our framework substantially expands the capabilities of birth–death models, providing a powerful and flexible approach to infer complex epidemiological and macroevolutionary processes.

title: Structural and biochemical impact of clinically relevant constitutively active parathyroid hormone receptor 1 mutations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Parathyroid hormone receptor 1 (PTH1R) constitutively active mutants, including H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P, are responsible for Jansen’s metaphyseal chondrodysplasia, a form of short-limbed dwarfism. Here, we expand pharmacological understanding and present cryoelectron microscopy structures of the constitutively active PTH1R mutants, H223
                    2.50
                    K, H223
                    2.50
                    R, and T410
                    6.42
                    P, in complex with Gs protein and PTH(1–34), and H223
                    2.50
                    R and T410
                    6.42
                    P in the ligand free Gs complexed form. These reveal modifications in polar networks that allow for constitutive G protein coupling and subsequent signaling. In the absence of a peptide bound to the extracellular side of the PTH1R, TM6 adopts a distinct conformation relative to the PTH(1–34) bound wild-type PTH1R coupled with Gs. Combined with molecular dynamics analysis of inactive and Gs bound receptors, this work reveals distinct mechanisms that lead to differing receptor activation states and consequently promote distinct constitutive activity and agonist-mediated pharmacological profiles.

title: Humans show limited ability to distinguish human-authored from AI-generated political content on social media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: This study employs a set of behavioral experiments to examine how individuals perceive the humanness of social media posts about the 2024 U.S. presidential debate between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump. Posts presented in the experiment were authored either by humans or chatbots, varying the large language model (LLM), the model architecture, the social media platform, and the political personas. Participants judged randomly paired posts to identify which they perceived to be AI-generated. We find that human-authored posts were on average perceived as more human-like than AI outputs generated from five of the six LLMs in this study. However, participants’ ability to detect AI-generated content is limited. They do so only slightly above chance in human–AI pairs, and this ability weakens for newer LLMs, varies by platform, and reflects partisan bias. Only posts generated with Llama 3.3 scored, on average, higher on perceived humanness than human-authored posts. The social media platform also mattered, with participants distinguishing human from AI on most platforms (YouTube, TikTok, Truth Social), but not on X/Twitter. Incivility and negative emotions are associated with high humanness perceptions, and partisan identity also shaped evaluations, with Republican respondents more likely to view ideologically misaligned AI posts as AI-generated.

title: Isotope evidence for changing methane sources at high northern latitudes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The renewed increase of methane (CH
                    4
                    ) in the atmosphere since 2007 is an imminent threat to the stability of the climate system and undermines climate policy goals. A reversal in the trend of its carbon isotopic composition (
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    ) in the 21st century indicates a fundamental shift in the global CH
                    4
                    cycle. Here, we investigate the origin of this
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    trend by determining isotope source signatures of CH
                    4
                    emissions based on high and mid-northern latitude observations. A clear latitude gradient and seasonal cycle of the source signatures reflect the spatially and temporally varying contributions of the different sources, each with distinct signatures. We find a large shift in the source signature after 2007 between −3.6 and −5.1‰ at high northern latitudes, and a moderate change between −0.4 and −0.9‰ at mid-northern latitudes. The decrease in
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    source signature is likely caused by a shift from thermogenic and pyrogenic to microbial sources, accompanied by a likely decrease in the isotopic signature of the microbial emissions, possibly resulting from climate change. Our results suggest that current inverse models may underestimate the shift between fossil and microbial emissions at high northern latitudes, or that microbial methanogenesis pathways change much more strongly than currently believed. Source changes at high latitudes have a disproportionate contribution to the observed trend in atmospheric
                    δ
                    13
                    C
                    CH4
                    .

title: Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
India routinely experiences some of the highest concentrations of fine particulate matter (PM
                    2.5
                    ) air pollution in the world. Although India’s population predominantly lives in rural areas and smaller cities, policy efforts to date have emphasized air pollution in India’s large cities. In contrast, there is limited understanding of air pollutant dynamics in India’s rural and less urbanized areas. Here, we established a well-calibrated lower-cost PM
                    2.5
                    sensor network spanning a wide range of urbanicity (population densities: 300 to 30,000 people/km
                    2
                    ) outside and inside of Delhi. The network of 49 sites incorporated a 160 km measurement transect to capture ambient PM
                    2.5
                    trends of the Delhi megacity, as well as stratified measurements in villages, small cities, and Delhi itself. We report on data from 5 mo of operation (July–November 2024) spanning the cleanest and most polluted times of the year. PM
                    2.5
                    concentrations at rural sites consistently exceeded those at urban sites by about 20% during every month of our study. Analysis of diurnal PM
                    2.5
                    cycles showed sharp morning (approximately 06:00–10:00 LT) and evening (approximately 16:00–20:00 LT) concentration peaks at rural sites that were absent at urban sites. We attribute these events to widespread use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry in suburban and rural settings. These striking enhancements in rural air pollution are missed by satellite remote sensing data, and our findings run contrary to the general societal perception that Indian cities are pollution hotspots relative to rural areas.

title: Rethinking broad diet breadth as a sign of scarcity: A 50,000-y record of subsistence from northwestern Australia
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The prey choice model, widely applied in archaeological reconstructions of Pleistocene diet, predicts that people will initially focus on a narrow suite of high-ranked prey before broadening their diet to include lower-ranked species as necessitated by subsistence needs. However, evidence from arid and semiarid northern Australia challenges this assumption. Archaeological faunal records demonstrate that a broad diet was established early and persisted through the Holocene. We argue that these diverse diets do not indicate resource scarcity, but rather represent an ideal strategy for exploiting abundant, low-risk hidden, or cryptic prey, as well as high-risk, conspicuous prey within an environment characterized by unpredictable rainfall. This pattern also necessitates reconceptualizing traditional notions of prey rank and dietary breadth. Rather than adhering to static prey rankings, northern Australian peoples skillfully adapted their hunting strategies in response to fluctuating nutritional content and pursuit costs of different species. The most successful subsistence strategy in this region was therefore one of high responsiveness and flexibility, manifesting as a consistently broad diet. This case study suggests that the relationship between human dietary breadth and resource abundance is more nuanced in situations of abundant, cryptic prey.

title: Synergistic Interface Lubrication and Anion Anchoring in a Composite Solid‐State Electrolyte for Dendrite‐Free and Wide‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid‐state zinc‐ion batteries are promising for safe and flexible energy storage but suffer from low ionic conductivity and poor interfacial contact of polymer electrolytes. Herein, we report a composite solid‐state electrolyte (CSE) integrating 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI) ionic liquid and boron nitride (BN) nanosheets into polyvinylidene fluoride hexafluoropropylene (PVDF‐HFP) matrix. EMIMTFSI acts as a plasticizer to suppress polymer crystallization, enhance ionic conductivity (5.23/0.76 mS cm
                    −1
                    at 30/−20°C), and improve interfacial contact. Concurrently, BN anchors TFSI
                    −
                    via Lewis acid‐base interactions, regulating Zn
                    2+
                    −TFSI
                    −
                    coordination and facilitating ion dissociation, thereby guiding uniform Zn deposition along the (002) orientation. This synergy endows CSE with a high Zn
                    2+
                    transference number (0.56) and a low activation energy (0.21 eV). Consequently, Zn//Zn cell cycles stablely for 2000 h at 0.5 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , and Zn//Cu cell delivers an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.75% for 1000 cycles. The Zn//hydrated aluminum vanadate (HAVO) full cell exhibits outstanding cycling stability (90.6% capacity retention after 6000 cycles), and stable operation at −20°C to 50°C. The Zn//HAVO pouch cell further demonstrates the practical viability of CSE in flexible electronics. This work presents a synergistic strategy for high‐performance polymer electrolytes, advancing the prospects of durable solid‐state zinc metal batteries.

title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell–tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.

title: NSP1–SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in
                    
                      Stat1
                      −/−
                    
                    pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1–SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1–SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in
                    
                      Samd9l
                      −/−
                    
                    mice. Combined deletion of
                    Samd9l
                    and
                    Stat1
                    permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.

title: A chromatin biology assessment of AlphaFold3
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold have achieved remarkable success in predicting structures of single proteins and multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold3 now incorporates the capability to model complexes containing nucleic acids and chemically modified side chains. Investigators can now predict structures of proteins bound to chromatin, where interactions with nucleosomal DNA and histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) converge to control genome function. To evaluate its robustness in modeling chromatin complexes, we benchmarked AlphaFold3 on 115 structures containing nucleosomes whose coordinates were released by the Protein Data Bank after the training set cutoff date. We find that AlphaFold3 excels at predicting interactions with the histone octamer core and with PTMs. By contrast, AlphaFold3 struggles to predict structures of chromatin factors that primarily engage nucleosomal DNA, notably transcription factors and chromatin remodelers. We also show that AlphaFold3 can faithfully recapitulate known PTM recognition patterns, matching experimentally determined specificity profiles. This assessment of the capabilities and limitations of AlphaFold3 in chromatin structural biology provides a roadmap for its effective application to studies of chromatin regulation and PTM readout, while identifying key areas for future refinement of algorithms for predicting interactions between proteins and nucleic acids.

title: Tumor cell–intrinsic E47 functions as a critical suppressor in antitumor immunity via the FBXL2–PD-L1 axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The transcription factor E47, encoded by the
                    TCF3
                    gene, is essential for B and T cell lineage commitment and development. However, whether tumor cell–intrinsic E47 contributes to tumor immunosurveillance remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that E47 functions as a critical suppressor of antitumor immunity. Clinical analyses reveal that increased intratumoral
                    TCF3
                    expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Silencing of E47 in tumor cells markedly inhibits tumor growth, increases infiltration of cytotoxic CD8
                    +
                    T cells, and decreases PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, E47 transcriptionally represses
                    FBXL2
                    , which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes PD-L1 polyubiquitination at K270 and proteasomal degradation. Restoration of FBXL2 effectively reverses E47-induced PD-L1 upregulation and tumor growth. Strikingly, Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug nebivolol, an activator of FBXL2, significantly enhances antitumor immunity and improves the efficacy of CTLA-4 blockade therapy in syngeneic tumor mouse models. Together, this study uncovers the E47–FBXL2 axis as a critical pathway governing PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for improving the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Topological validation of generated scientific images
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Synthetic data have become an indispensable tool for validation, standards development, and product design across a broad range of scientific and engineering disciplines. One of the earliest examples arose in energy systems, where security and confidentiality constraints motivated the development of synthetic power grids and, in turn, novel topological and geometric approaches for evaluating their fidelity. Today, synthetic scientific imagery has emerged as a new critical tool in a variety of applications, ranging from autonomous driving, robotics, and Internet-of-Things technologies to in silico trials, digital twins, and remote sensing of environment. Yet the rigorous assessment of such synthetic images and quantification of their associated uncertainties remains a fundamental challenge. Building on the recent advances in the topological and geometric validation of synthetic power grids, we develop a systematic framework for comparing image data through the persistence of their multiscale shape patterns using the statistical formalism of survival analysis. While the tools of persistent homology and statistical survival analysis are both mature methodologies, they have so far developed largely in isolation. Unlike more traditional comparison methods such as pixel-level similarity or distributional summaries that often fail to capture the complex, multiscale structural characteristics of modern scientific imagery, our approach shows the capability to systematically assess the mismatch between different images at all scales simultaneously, while characterizing the associated uncertainty. The resulting synergistic methodology establishes a broadly applicable statistical topological framework for validating synthetic scientific imagery and, more generally, complex synthetic data products.

title: Conditions for runaway ruptures during reservoir operations: Magnitude–frequency distribution implications and application to Groningen
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a theoretical analysis of an induced seismic rupture propagating from a gas reservoir into the underburden. We use linear elastic fracture mechanics to determine the conditions for self-arrested or runaway ruptures. We derive a phase diagram in which the model parameters (the reservoir thickness, the reservoir pressure depletion, background stress, and fracture energy) are combined into two dimensionless parameters. We apply the analysis to the seismicity induced by gas extraction from the Groningen gas field, where earthquakes have remained confined to the close vicinity of the reservoir. We invert the observations for the model parameters. They indicate subcritical initial stress on the underburden faults, meaning that runaway ruptures are possible in principle, but the conditions required for such events to have happened were most likely not met in reality. The model reproduces the spatial and temporal patterns of observed maximum earthquake magnitudes, and the significant deficit of
                    M
                    > 3.0 events compared to the expectation from the Gutenberg–Richter relationship. This tapering implies that the expected maximum magnitude is nearly insensitive to the total number of induced earthquakes and strongly controlled by the reservoir thickness and pressure depletion. Because the forecast is probabilistic and accounts for uncertainties in the model parameters, it does not exclude runaway ruptures; but such events are found to be unlikely. The model offers an operational framework to forecast earthquake magnitudes by constraining the physical model with measurable parameters.

title: Protein spherical nucleic acids enable multivalent display of TLR9 agonists for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Precise control over nanoparticle composition and molecular architecture remains a fundamental challenge in nanomedicine, limiting systematic exploration of therapeutic design and biological function. Here, we report structurally defined protein spherical nucleic acids (ProSNAs) comprising ferritin nanocages densely functionalized with Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, immunostimulatory oligonucleotide shell for cancer immunotherapy. ProSNAs are rapidly internalized by immune cells, elicit potent innate immune activation, and exhibit prolonged intratumoral retention with preferential uptake by myeloid cells. These responses promote dendritic cell maturation, polarize macrophages toward an antitumor phenotype, and stimulate robust CD8
                    +
                    T cell–mediated immunity. Across murine melanoma, colon adenocarcinoma, and triple-negative breast cancer models, a single intratumoral administration of ProSNAs induces durable tumor regression, suppresses metastatic progression, and synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade. Taken together, these findings establish ProSNAs as a structurally defined, myeloid-targeting nanomedicine platform for programmable cancer immunotherapy.

title: Reducing belief in conspiracy theories as they unfold using large language models
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The emergence of conspiracy theories in the wake of major events is a significant societal challenge. Here, we test whether conversational dialogues with a large language model (LLM) can reduce belief in immediately unfolding conspiracies. In experiments conducted in the days following the July 2024 assassination attempt on Donald Trump and the September 2025 assassination of Charlie Kirk, US adults (Experiment 1: N = 472; Experiment 2: N = 1,042) holding conspiratorial views about the crisis event engaged in a multiturn conversation with an LLM prompted to reduce their conspiracy belief. Compared to control participants who either discussed an irrelevant topic with an LLM or viewed a static fact sheet, participants in the LLM treatment showed significantly reduced conspiracy beliefs in both experiments. We also found suggestive evidence of downstream effects of the LLM treatment, observing reduced belief in some—but not all—analyses of different conspiratorial beliefs 1 to 2 mo later. These results shed light on the psychology of emerging conspiracies and highlight the potential for scalable, information-focused LLM interventions to counteract misinformation in the immediate aftermath of high-profile societal events.

title: A decavalent Group B streptococcal biosynthetic conjugate vaccine provides functional immunity to all known serotypes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Globally, 394,000 cases of Group B
                    Streptococcus
                    (GBS) infection occur each year, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Vaccination has emerged as an important strategy to limit GBS infections and disease; however, existing vaccine candidates currently in clinical development do not cover all capsular polysaccharide serotypes. Here, we describe the use of a next generation bioconjugation platform to generate a decavalent GBS vaccine (GBS10V) and characterize its immunological evaluation in animals. Using an evolved PglS bioconjugation platform, capsular polysaccharides from all 10 GBS capsular polysaccharide serotypes were individually expressed and bioconjugated to an optimized
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    exotoxin A (EPA6) carrier protein engineered with six sequons. Multiple biochemical analyses confirmed the identity of each polysaccharide serotype bioconjugated to EPA6. Moreover, intact mass spectrometry (MS) and MS/MS spectra confirmed the presence of sialic acid in each repeat unit of GBS polysaccharides attached to the carrier, an attribute critical for eliciting an optimal immune response. The GBS10V vaccine was used to immunize outbred CD-1 mice and New Zealand White rabbits with doses of 1, 2, or 5 μg per GBS serotype. Sera analyses demonstrated the GBS10V vaccine induced high serotype-specific immunoglobulin titers to all 10 serotypes. Most importantly, interim and postimmune sera from rabbits demonstrated potent opsonophagocytic killing, with median titers ranging from 646 to 6,145 for all serotypes by day 42. Together, these findings establish GBS10V as a global GBS conjugate vaccine candidate for all patient populations, and thus, justify its further preclinical development.

title: Inactivation of the RB1 and PTPN14 tumor suppressors cooperatively enables the lifespan extension activity of the human papillomavirus E7 oncoprotein
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) E7 proteins bind and inactivate host cellular tumor suppressors and are essential for the immortalization of primary human keratinocytes. E7 proteins from high- and low-risk HPV genotypes bind directly to at least two tumor suppressors, RB1 and PTPN14, and inactivate both. We previously characterized mutations in high-risk HPV E7 proteins that selectively abrogate the ability of E7 to bind either RB1 or PTPN14.
